'''Hong Chaosheng''' ({{zh|c=洪朝生|p=Hóng Cháoshēng|w='''Hung Ch'ao-sheng'''}}; 10 October 1920 – 19 August 2018) was a Chinese [[physicist]] best known for studying [[cryogenics]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Professor HONG Chaosheng |url=http://english.ipc.cas.cn/pe/cm/200708/t20070815_1348.html |access-date=6 October 2018 |work=ipc.cas.cn |date=2018 |archive-date=5 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180805012015/http://english.ipc.cas.cn/pe/cm/200708/t20070815_1348.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Hong was the teacher of [[Zhao Zhongxian]], a laureate of [[Highest Science and Technology Award]], the highest scientific award issued by the Chinese Academy of Sciences to scientists working in China.

He was a delegate to the [[3rd National People's Congress]]. He was a member of the 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th National Committee of the [[Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference]].

==Biography==
Hong was born in [[Beijing]] on October 10, 1920, to Hong Guantao ({{zh|s=洪观涛|t=|links=no}}), a railway engineer and member of [[Tongmenghui]], and Gao Junyuan ({{zh|s=高君远|t=|links=no}}), daughter of publisher Gao Mengdan ({{zh|s=高梦旦|t=|links=no}}).<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sohu.com/a/250340022_372479 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006194654/http://www.sohu.com/a/250340022_372479 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |script-title=zh:李来风：我的恩师洪朝生先生 |work=Sohu |date=2018-08-27 |language=zh }}</ref> He had two elder sisters, Hong Jing ({{zh|s=洪晶|t=|links=no}}) and [[Hong Ying]] ({{zh|s=洪盈|t=|links=no}}). He primarily studied at the Yuying School ({{zh|s=育英学校|t=|links=no}}) and secondary studied at Huiwen High School ({{zh|s=汇文学校|t=|links=no}}), both were missionary schools.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.guancha.cn/industry-science/2018_08_20_468817_1.shtml |script-title=zh:98岁中科院院士洪朝生去世：我国低温物理开创者 |work=guancha.cn |date=2018-08-20 |language=zh}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sohu.com/a/250339948_372479 |script-title=zh:送别低温王国拓荒人：洪朝生先生 |work=Sohu |date=2018-08-27 |language=zh |access-date=2018-10-06 |archive-date=2018-10-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006104650/http://www.sohu.com/a/250339948_372479 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  After high school, he studied at [[Tsinghua University]], and then taught at [[National Southwestern Associated University]]. He arrived in the [[United States]] in 1945 at the age of 25 to begin his education at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]]. After university, he worked at [[Purdue University]]. In 1950 he went to [[Netherlands]] to work at [[Leiden University]].<ref name="bee">{{cite news|url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_2362886 |script-title=zh:著名物理学家、中国低温物理和低温技术研究开创者洪朝生逝世 |work=thepaper.cn |date=2018-08-20 |language=zh}}</ref><ref name="elephant">{{cite news|url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/science/2016-08/24/c_135629540.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006223452/http://www.xinhuanet.com/science/2016-08/24/c_135629540.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 6, 2018 |script-title=zh:洪朝生：科研有道，育人有方 |work=Xinhuanet |date=2016-08-24 |language=zh}}</ref>

He returned to China in 1952 and that year became professor of Department of Physics at Tsinghua University, [[Peking University]] and the [[University of Science and Technology of China]]. He joined the [[Jiusan Society]]. In 1953, he became a researcher at the Institute of Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, where he was deputy director in 1978. He was accepted as an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1980. In September 2005, he was hired as a part-time professor at the Graduate College of Chinese Academy of Sciences.<ref name="bee"/><ref name="elephant"/>

On August 19, 2018, he died of illness at Beijing, aged 98.<ref name="bee"/>

==Personal life==
Hong married Li Ying ({{zh|s=李滢|t=|links=no}}).
